verification.notes: Draft, not reviewed by a NERDC, UBEC or Federal Ministry of Education officer. The subject lists and the minimum and maximum number of subjects per stage are read from the NERDC revised 9-year curriculum strategy document and are the pack's firmest data. Open items: (1) the A1 to F9 percentage ranges follow spec 03 Appendix G and secondary sources; no WAEC or NECO document fetched for this pack states them, and WAEC grades each subject by its own award, so the table is a school default. (2) The split of 40 continuous-assessment marks (two assessments of 20) and 60 examination marks is the common school practice named in spec 03 Appendix G; the UBEC FAQ, read from the search index only, gives the basic-education split as 60 for school-based assessment and 40 for the external examination. Both are overridable. (3) Primary schools often grade A to F with descriptors; no official boundaries were found, so primary uses the same nine-grade scale. (4) Nursery and pre-primary levels are not modelled. (5) Promotion is a class-council suggestion at an average of 40, the lowest passing grade on the scale; Nigeria publishes no national promotion rule that this pack cites. (6) Typical term dates are pre-fills only; the state ministry publishes the session calendar. (7) The Hausa labels are a draft translation that no native speaker has reviewed.
